details.description: GPT Audio is OpenAI's first generally available audio model for the Chat Completions API, accepting and producing both text and audio in a single, non-realtime request rather than a persistent low-latency session. It is designed for asynchronous audio workloads such as text-to-speech generation and audio summarization, and the 2025-08-28 snapshot covered here is its original release. OpenAI is retiring GPT Audio on January 20, 2027 and recommends migrating to gpt-audio-1.5.
advantages: Accepts and returns both audio and text in a single call through the standard Chat Completions API, distinct from the low-latency gpt-realtime model built for persistent WebSocket sessions (OpenAI API docs; Microsoft Learn).
Supports function calling and streaming responses (OpenAI API docs).
disadvantages: OpenAI is retiring GPT Audio on January 20, 2027, with gpt-audio-1.5 as the recommended replacement (OpenAI API deprecations page).
Only works through the Chat Completions endpoint; not compatible with Realtime, Live sessions, Assistants, Batch, fine-tuning or embeddings (OpenAI API docs).
Knowledge cutoff of October 1, 2023 (OpenAI API docs).
use_cases: Asynchronous, non-realtime audio conversations built on Chat Completions
Voice features that do not require real-time, low-latency responses

notes: The catalog groups this target under a single dated Azure snapshot (azure/gpt-audio-2025-08-28) of OpenAI's gpt-audio model. OpenAI's own deprecations page lists a January 20, 2027 shutdown for gpt-audio; the catalog's facts give a later date (2027-03-02), which may reflect an Azure-specific retirement schedule I could not independently confirm, so the catalog's date is kept and only the OpenAI-documented date is stated above. No accuracy-style benchmark for this model was found on any maker, host or third-party page.
